title: Ordinary resolution rules on Noetherian quasi-excellent rational schemes
statement: Let the inputs be all reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth] over $\mathbf Q$ whose affine coordinate rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], using the affine-local predicate of [def-per-gabber-modification-data]. A regular morphism $f:Y\to X$ between inputs is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and, for every $x\in X$ and every finite field extension $K/\kappa(x)$, the scheme $Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]; here $\kappa(x)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and the fibre product is as in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. An ordinary regular-functorial resolution rule assigns each input an ordinary blowup tower [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule], with coherent ideal centers [pqf-def-coherent] whose closed subschemes are nonempty, nowhere dense and regular, and with regular last scheme. For every regular morphism over $\mathbf Q$, it specifies the ordered cartesian contracted-pullback comparison of [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule]: the retained ideals are the extended ideals, and exactly unit ideals are deleted. The comparison counts and level maps respect identities and composition. For a surjective regular morphism all stages are retained. The empty input has length zero. No finite-type, separation or finite-dimension condition is imposed; finite disjoint unions are included in the input domain.

source.place: VIII 2.1.12, 2.3.1, 2.3.4, Remark 2.3.5(i) and Theorem 2.3.10, printed pp.88,91--93
